source.title: How Does Topology of Neural Architectures Impact Gradient Propagation and Model Performance
source.authors: K. Bhardwaj; Gui-Hong Li; R. Marculescu

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary information are present. Some extracted page text is garbled or duplicated, but the relevant experimental descriptions and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how architecture topology and NN-Mass relate to test accuracy and initial gradient properties, but does not measure the training-to-test error gap or directly test a listed version.
record.gate_note: The reported NN-Mass and test-accuracy relationships are results of this study. Values used only to select or design architectures, and DARTS results cited from prior work, are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests relationships among skip-connection topology, NN-Mass, initial Jacobian singular values, convergence and test accuracy. None measures a V1–V8 effect. In particular, initial gradient propagation is not magnitude-aware sharpness, and varying CNN width does not establish behavior beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors theoretically connect NN-Mass to initial layerwise gradient propagation for their DenseNet-type setup, empirically associate matched NN-Mass and width with similar convergence and accuracy, extend the accuracy analysis to other skip-connection families, and demonstrate architecture compression. These findings do not establish any V1–V8 effect.
record.recipe_differences: Studies randomly generated DenseNet-type skip topologies and relates NN-Mass, initialization gradient properties, and test accuracy; it does not test random-label memorization, interpolation thresholds, or training-to-test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported relationships vary with width; at width multiplier 1, 31-layer CNNs did not cluster into NN-Mass buckets. The paper also cautions that comparisons across widths are not warranted by its same-width theory.

fits_no_version.finding: NN-Mass fits test accuracy better than parameter count in the reported architecture families, with weaker clustering for narrow, shallow CNNs and comparisons generally conditioned on width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within the tested architecture families and width conditions, NN-Mass helps identify networks with similar held-out accuracy despite different depths and parameter counts.

fits_no_version.finding: NN-Mass correlates with initial Jacobian singular values; matched NN-Mass and width accompany similar convergence, while higher NN-Mass accompanies faster convergence in the reported comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NN-Mass and width track initial gradient propagation and training convergence in the tested MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: Different-depth CNNs attain comparable accuracy at different NN-Densities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NN-Density alone does not identify equally accurate CNNs across depths.

fits_no_version.finding: NN-Mass-selected smaller CNNs attain accuracy close to larger reference models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NN-Mass can guide architecture compression with small accuracy changes in the reported CIFAR-10 and ImageNet examples.

record.problems: The study does not report training-to-test gaps. Much of the architecture-performance evidence is presented as fit statistics and plotted clustering; numeric per-architecture values are not all given in text. For ResNets and WRNs, the study reuses published accuracy and parameter counts and performs no training. Hyperparameters for smaller models were not individually optimized, which the authors say could reduce accuracy gaps.
record.rows_left_out: The MLP comparisons for model groups (D,E,F) and (F,G,H) are described as similar observations but lack separate numeric details in the supplied text; omitted to avoid duplicating qualitative aggregate results in R3–R4. Additional figure-only clusters and FLOPS plots in Figures 17–19 are not entered separately where the text provides no separate numeric result beyond the related architecture findings already recorded.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fixed-random-label training, memorization capacity, and held-out performance under both label conditions.
Test error as width increases beyond the width yielding zero training error in converged networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, learned locality, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and the effects of tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and changes to training duration or recipe.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, varying dropout strength, dataset size, and joint removal of weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus training-to-test gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because no row measures a listed effect; this does not negate the reported NN-Mass findings. No version-specific verdicts are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train the same architectures and recipes on natural and fixed random labels.
Does not sweep one-hidden-layer ReLU networks past the zero-training-error threshold or report double descent.
Does not compare fully connected and convolutional networks on the same image tasks or isolate local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not vary batch size or test large-batch generalization.
Does not vary dropout or weight decay.
Measures initial layerwise Jacobian singular values and NN-Mass against test accuracy, not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance against the training-to-test gap.
Does not identify or remove memorized training examples.

rows.subject: Random MLP architectures (wc = 8)
rows.operation_detail: Varied depth and random concatenation skip-connection count; compared test accuracy with parameter count and NN-Mass on MNIST.
rows.measure: Test accuracy versus log(NN-Mass) and log(#Params); goodness of fit R2.
rows.note: Reports an aggregate fit across the tested MLP architectures; no training-to-test error gap is reported.
rows.check: The fit statistics concern NN-Mass, not a listed effect. Figure 3 reports test-accuracy standard deviations of approximately 0.05–0.34%, omitted from the row.

rows.subject: Random MLP architectures (wc = 8)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean singular values of initial layerwise Jacobians against NN-Mass and parameter count.
rows.measure: Goodness of fit between mean singular values and architecture measure, R2.
rows.note: This measures initial gradient geometry, not the training-to-test gap.
rows.check: Initial Jacobian singular values measure gradient propagation, not V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or generalization gap.

rows.subject: Models X and Y
rows.operation_detail: Compared training convergence for models with similar NN-Mass but different depth and parameter count.
rows.measure: Training accuracy versus epochs; curves nearly coincide.
rows.value: Training convergence of model X nearly coincides with model Y.
rows.note: The text states the qualitative comparison; no numeric convergence values are given.
rows.check: Similar training convergence at matched NN-Mass does not measure any listed effect.

rows.subject: Models Z and Y
rows.operation_detail: Compared training convergence for models with similar parameter count but different depth and NN-Mass.

conditions.value: Z has higher NN-Mass than Y

rows.measure: Training accuracy versus epochs; convergence speed.
rows.value: Model Z has significantly faster training convergence than Y.
rows.note: The paper attributes the faster convergence to higher NN-Mass and better LDI.
rows.check: Faster training convergence at higher NN-Mass does not measure any listed effect. Z and Y have approximately similar parameter counts, 8.3K versus 9.0K.

rows.subject: DenseNet-type CNNs (width multiplier wm = 2)
rows.size_stated: models range from 5M to 9M parameters in the described box; several depths
rows.operation_detail: Varied depth and random concatenation skip connections; compared test accuracy against parameter count and NN-Mass on CIFAR-10.

conditions.value: mean of three runs; std. dev. ∼ 0.1%

rows.measure: Test accuracy versus NN-Mass; reported linear-fit R2.
rows.locator: Section 4.3; Figure 5 and Appendix H.5, Figure 16
rows.note: Architecture groups are reported in aggregate; the paper says test accuracies cluster by NN-Mass despite different sizes.
rows.check: These are accuracy fits against log(parameter count) and log(NN-Mass), not a listed effect; specify the logarithms in the measure.

rows.subject: DenseNet-type CNNs (width multiplier wm = 3)
rows.size_stated: models include 6M–7M parameter models and models up to 16M parameters
rows.operation_detail: Varied depth and random concatenation skip connections; compared test accuracy against parameter count and NN-Mass on CIFAR-10.

conditions.value: mean of three runs; std. dev. ∼ 0.1%

rows.measure: Test accuracy goodness of fit against log(parameter count) and log(NN-Mass).
rows.note: The paper describes parameter counting as completely failing to predict accuracy at this width.
rows.check: The architecture-fit comparison does not measure a listed effect or establish a post-interpolation width trend.

rows.subject: DenseNet-type CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy of different-depth CNNs against NN-Density on CIFAR-10.
rows.measure: Test accuracy across depth and NN-Density; qualitative comparison.
rows.value: A 31-layer model with ρavg = 0.3 performs close to a 64-layer model with ρavg = 0.1; a 49-layer model with ρavg = 0.2 outperforms the 64-layer model.
rows.locator: Appendix H.2, Impact of Varying NN-Density; Figure 13
rows.note: Shows NN-Density alone does not identify models with similar accuracy across depths.
rows.check: The result concerns the inadequacy of NN-Density for matching accuracy across depths, not any listed version.

rows.subject: DenseNet-type CNNs (width multiplier wm = 1)
rows.operation_detail: Compared test-accuracy clustering across model depths and NN-Mass on CIFAR-10.
rows.value: 31-layer models do not fall within the buckets; the authors hypothesize their capacity is too small to reach high accuracy.
rows.locator: Appendix H.3, Varying width multiplier on CIFAR-10; Figure 14(a,b)
rows.note: The stated explanation is a hypothesis; no numerical accuracy values for these particular models are given in text.
rows.check: Incomplete clustering qualifies the authors' NN-Mass finding, not a listed version. The capacity explanation is explicitly a hypothesis.

rows.subject: DenseNet-type CNNs
rows.size_stated: models with width multipliers wm = 1, 2, and 3; multiple depths
rows.operation_detail: Compared goodness of fit of test accuracy to log(NN-Mass) as width changes on CIFAR-10.
rows.measure: R2 for test accuracy fit against log(NN-Mass).
rows.note: The paper reports increasing fit as width increases.
rows.check: Increasing fit quality across widths does not show that widening beyond zero training error keeps lowering test error.

rows.subject: DenseNet-type CNNs
rows.size_stated: four-cell CNNs; total depth ∈ {48, 56, 60, 64, 68}; width multiplier wm ∈ {1.5, 2}
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy of architectures with different parameter counts and NN-Mass on ImageNet.
rows.measure: Test accuracy similarity and clustering by NN-Mass.
rows.value: Models {P,Q}, {W,X}, and {Y,Z} have very different #Params but similar test accuracy; models of different widths are not compared within the same cluster.
rows.note: The paper explicitly limits cross-width comparisons because the theory requires both same width and NN-Mass.
rows.check: Within-width accuracy clustering does not measure a listed effect. The cross-width restriction qualifies the NN-Mass comparison, not V1–V8.

rows.subject: DenseNet-type CNNs with depthwise separable convolutions
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy against parameter count and NN-Mass on CIFAR-10.
rows.measure: Goodness of fit between test accuracy and architecture measure, R2.
rows.note: The text reports the aggregate fit across the tested DSConv models.
rows.check: The NN-Mass fit for depthwise-separable CNNs does not compare convolutional and fully connected architectures or measure another listed effect.

rows.subject: Standard ResNets and Wide-ResNets
rows.size_stated: RN-50, WRN-34-1.5, WRN18-3; 26M–101M parameters for the cited group
rows.operation_detail: Related NN-Mass to reported ImageNet Top1 accuracy for standard ResNets and WRNs; the authors did not train these models.

conditions.value: accuracy and #Params taken directly from Tables 7,8 in the Wide-ResNet paper

rows.measure: Goodness of fit of Top1 accuracy against parameter count and NN-Mass, R2.
rows.note: The paper states no training was performed for these ResNet/WRN results.
rows.check: The underlying accuracies and parameter counts are cited results, not newly trained models. The NN-Mass fit is this study's own secondary analysis; retain only with that attribution.

rows.subject: MobileNet-v2 and newly sampled CNNs
rows.size_stated: MobileNet-v2 width multipliers 0.75 and 1.4; newly sampled CNNs use Nc = 22
rows.operation_detail: Related ImageNet Top1 accuracy to parameter count and NN-Mass.
rows.measure: Goodness of fit of Top1 accuracy against parameter count and NN-Mass, R2.
rows.note: The paper reports the aggregate fit across the plotted models.
rows.check: The pooled architecture-performance fit does not measure a listed effect.

rows.subject: NN-Mass-based DenseNet-type CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Trained smaller NN-Mass-selected CNNs and measured CIFAR-10 test accuracy.

conditions.value: mean ± standard deviation of three runs

rows.baseline: Manual model: 11.89M parameters, 3.63G FLOPS, 97.02%; manual model: 8.15M parameters, 2.54G FLOPS, 96.99%.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation of three runs; numeric deviations not stated in table text.
rows.note: These are compression outcomes, not a direct test of any listed claim version.
rows.check: This is performance of the study's own architecture-selection method against reference models; exclude as a claim-test row.

rows.subject: NN-Mass-based MobileNet-like models A and B
rows.size_stated: A: 3.7M parameters, 393M MACs; B: 2.3M parameters, 200M MACs
rows.operation_detail: Trained NN-Mass-selected compressed models and measured ImageNet Top1 accuracy.
rows.baseline: MobileNetV2 (1.4): 73.3 Top1, 6.1M parameters, 601M MACs; MobileNetV2 (0.75): 67.9 Top1, 2.6M parameters, 220M MACs.
rows.value: Model A: 72.9 Top1, 3.7M parameters, 393M MACs; model B: 68.56 Top1, 2.3M parameters, 200M MACs.
rows.note: Compression comparison; not a direct test of any listed claim version.
rows.check: This is performance of the study's own compression method against MobileNet references; exclude as a claim-test row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
